steps.line: We just moved here! Grandma won't unpack a thing until she's had tea, and her lucky spoon bounced out of the van near {next}.
Found it, a bit grassy but lucky as ever. Tomi ran ahead to set up the kitchen at {next}.
Grandma says the spoon only goes in the yellow cup with the chipped handle, she's had it forty years. I'll go tell her, meet us at {next}.
Ah, my spoon! Now, children of the new street, which cup do I take my tea in?
options: The blue mug with the cat on it
The tall glass with the straw
The yellow cup with the chipped handle
steps.wrong: Hmm, no, that's Tomi's cup. Mine has some history to it.
steps.right: Forty years, that cup. Come, the kettle's on at {next}.

steps.line: Tea in my cup, with my spoon, in my new town. Now it's home. Take some biscuits, I baked too many on purpose.
It's my first day at the new school tomorrow and I don't know the way! Ada says she knows, but Ada also said the moon was cheese. Start at {next}?
Okay I don't actually know the way. But I heard a kid say the school is the place where bells ring and nobody's in trouble for running at break.

steps.hint: Bells, books and running at break
steps.line: This is it! Tomi dropped his name sticker on the walk though, it's got a rocket on it. It blew toward {next}.
TOMI, with a rocket. Perfect. Grandma's waiting at {next} to hear how the practice walk went.
You walked it once, so tomorrow it's an old road. Here, a notebook for the first day. Write your new friends in it.
Grandma thinks nobody's coming to her housewarming. We invited the whole street! Shh. Tomi has the plan at {next}.
Quick test so you don't spoil it. What does Grandma think is happening tonight?
steps.wrong: No! She thinks nobody's coming, that's the whole surprise.
steps.right: Right, she thinks it's just us. Now we need decorations, the street said to meet at {next}.

steps.line: Everyone pitched in! Bring it all back here and we'll wrap the whole lot up, then off to {next}.
What is all this? The whole street? Oh, you rascals. Come in, all of you, I'll need more cups.

hunt.line: We just need three more bits: the {items}. Off you go!

steps.line: You're live on 98.6 The Breeze! Today's treasure hunt clue comes from a listener, head over to {next} and they'll read it out.
Hi Rosa, long time listener! My clue: go where the water slides under your feet but your feet stay dry.
Got it! Rosa says the prize is taped somewhere near {next}. Warmer, colder, she'll play along on air.
The ticket! Bring it to Rosa's outdoor booth at {next} and claim it live.
And our winners are on the line, folks! Here's your prize, a classic record. Next week's hunt is twice as tricky, stay tuned.
Breeze FM, week two! This time three listeners each hid a piece of my studio jukebox. First caller is waiting at {next}.
Rosa, dear, I hid mine years ago, I mean this morning. My grandkids helped. Rosa wants you to regroup at {next}.
You found all three! That's the record, the needle and the little crank. Bring them to the station van at {next}.
It plays! Listeners, the jukebox is fixed, and our hunters get one of their own. Next week: the grand prize.

hunt.line: The callers hid the {items}. Split up and bring them back!

steps.line: It's the grand prize hunt! Our oldest listener, Mr. Abara, has the first clue at {next}. He's been calling in since radio was black and white.
Ahem. Clue one, for Rosa. The prize waits where people look far and the city looks small.

steps.hint: Look far, the city looks small
steps.line: Rosa's on the phone: a second caller swears she saw the prize box colour. Talk to her at {next}.
I saw Rosa carrying it, it was green with a gold ribbon. Not the red one, that's her lunch. Rosa is at {next}.
Three boxes, live on air! Which one holds the grand prize?
options: The green box with a gold ribbon
steps.wrong: That's... my lunch, actually. Listeners, they almost ate my sandwich.
steps.right: The green box! The grand prize is buried treasure, folks, and the map's inside. It ends at {next}.

steps.line: Our hunters found it! Thank you to every caller who played along this season. This is Rosa on The Breeze, signing off happy.
I've got forty parcels and two legs. Can you take this one? The label got rained on, it just says PEMB... and 'loves tulips'. Try {next}.
Tulips? That's Mrs. Pemberton for sure, she plants them every year, the red ones. She walks her poodle near {next} about now.
Three Pembertons live on this street, believe it or not. Which one are you after?
options: Mrs. Pemberton who grows red tulips
Little Pip Pemberton who likes trains
steps.wrong: Nice try, but that one's got nothing to do with flowers.
steps.right: That's my wife! She's waiting for a parcel at {next}, she's been checking the window all morning.

steps.line: My bulbs! Next spring the whole street goes red. Here, take this bag, every good courier needs one.
Excuse me, I'm visiting and my guidebook is for a different city entirely. Would you show me around? I'd love to start at {next}.
Wonderful! My book says this is a cathedral in Prague. It is not. Next I want somewhere tall to see everything, like the riddle on my map: 'where the whole town fits in one look'.

steps.hint: The whole town in one look
steps.line: Splendid view! Now I'm hungry. Henrik's stomach says {next}.
Delicious. I've written postcards to everyone back home about this place. One last stop to post them, {next}?
Best tour I ever had, and I didn't even need my wrong book. I'll send you a postcard too!
Fun run today! Someone grazed a knee on the finish line and my kit is nearly empty. Can you help? My co-volunteer Sam is at {next}.
Kiko left spare supplies all over town, classic Kiko. While you're gone I'll make the runners some sweet tea. Back to {next} when you're done.
All restocked! One plaster with dinosaurs, one very brave runner. Come say hi at {next}.
Dinosaur plaster, best part of the race. I came last but I came happy. Here, my lucky snack, you've earned it.

hunt.line: I need the {items}. Thank you, heroes!

steps.line: Morning! There's a cat on a low branch who just won't come down. Not stuck, just stubborn. His owner is at {next}.
Biscuit? He only comes down for the jingle of his collar bell. He shook it off near {next} this morning, cheeky thing.
Jingle jingle. Pip is waiting with the short ladder at {next}.
Right, ladder's up. How do we get Biscuit down?
steps.wrong: Biscuit gives you a long, unimpressed look. Mrs. Ilsa said what he likes.
steps.right: He's coming! Down the ladder like a little king. Mrs. Ilsa says he has somewhere important to be, {next}.

steps.line: Turns out Biscuit is sort of the local mayor. Everyone on the street feeds him. He just wanted a better view of his town.
Six dogs, twelve ears, one of me. Waffles the dachshund slipped his lead to chase a smell. He loves cheese. Try {next}.
A tiny long dog? He sat here staring at the cheese counter for ten minutes, then trotted toward {next}. He left a little bandana behind.
Smells very much like cheese. Remy is waiting with the other five at {next}.
I've got a treat bag here. Which treat will bring Waffles running?
steps.wrong: Waffles is not interested. You know his weakness.
steps.right: Cheese! That got his attention. I hear tiny feet heading to {next}.

steps.line: Waffles! Six dogs, all present. Waffles wants you to know he was never lost, he was investigating.
My bike gave up halfway across town. Chain off, bell gone, tyre flat. The repair lady at {next} might have parts.
I don't have parts, but I know who does. Bring them back to {next} and Tomasz can fix it himself, I'll supervise.
Chain on, bell on, tyre patched! Ding ding. Ride with me to {next}, I owe you.
I was lost and broken down, now I'm just lost. Here, my old compass, maybe it'll work better for you.

hunt.line: Get the {items}. Tell them Hattie sent you!

steps.line: The wedding starts at noon and the rings are... somewhere. Little Leo, the ring bearer, was practising walking with them. He went to feed ducks.
There's Leo, covered in breadcrumbs. He says he put the ring box down by {next} so it wouldn't fall in.
Two rings, safe and sound. Leo wants to carry them back himself. The groom is pacing at {next}.
You found them! Fenella's in a flap. Who was holding them all morning?
steps.wrong: Hmm, no, they gave them to someone small and serious.
steps.right: Leo! Good lad, he was being careful. Let's get everyone to {next}.

steps.line: Rings, ring bearer, couple, cake. Everything's here. Have a flower from the bouquet, you saved my whole day.
I can't find my dad. He's got a big orange hat and he laughs like a goose. We were going to {next}.
Orange hat? He bought two buns and asked if anyone had seen a girl with a dino backpack. He went to {next}.
There are three men waiting around here. Which one is Maya's dad?
options: The tall man in a blue cap
The man with an orange hat, laughing like a goose
The man in a green scarf reading a paper
steps.wrong: Maya shakes her head. Not him, his hat's all wrong.
steps.right: DAD! Honk honk, there's the laugh. He says to meet him at {next}, he's buying everyone a treat.

steps.line: I turned round for one second to look at a pigeon. Thank you both. Here, one of the buns is yours.
Inside: a library card, a punch card for a bakery and a photo of a parrot in a tiny hat. Ask at {next}.
That's Mr. Osei's card. He reads only parrot books, I am not exaggerating. He goes to the bakery at {next} every day.
Mr. Osei? Nine stamps, one more for a free cake! He sits with his parrot at {next} after lunch.

steps.npc: An old man on a bench
steps.line: A wallet? Several of us lost things today. What's in it, so I know it's mine?
options: A parrot photo and a library card
A bus pass and a lucky coin
steps.wrong: That's not mine, I'm afraid. Mine's got my bird in it.
steps.right: That's Captain, my parrot! Thank you. Come with me to {next}, cake is on me.

steps.line: The tenth stamp! Free cake for everyone. Captain says thank you too. Well, he says 'hello sailor', but he means thank you.
A gust took my song sheets! I wrote that song for my old band and I can't remember the chorus. My friend at {next} saw where they went.
Three pages, flying three directions. I'll save Delphine a coffee. Bring them back to {next}.
Verse, verse, chorus! I've texted the old band, they're coming to {next} to play it together.
Ten years since we played this together. Same song, sore fingers, big smiles. This one's for you.

hunt.line: The pages landed far apart: the {items}.

steps.line: Marathon day! Water station seven is out of cups. The supply cart left a box at {next}, could you fetch it?
Cups! Runner number 42 asked for squash, not water, she was very clear. Take them back to {next}.
Hello again! Did you remember what I wanted?
steps.wrong: She laughs and keeps jogging on the spot. Not quite, it was fruity.
steps.right: Squash, perfect! She runs off waving. Gwen says the finish line party is at {next}.

steps.line: Every runner made it and every cup got used. Best station on the course. Have some melon, volunteers' privilege.
The farmers' market opens in an hour and I'm missing half my stall! My neighbour Basil is at {next}, he'll know.
Agnes leaves things everywhere. Last week she left a goose. When you've got them, set up at {next}.
Bunting up, sign written, bell ringing! The market's open. The pie stall is at {next}, come taste.
First pie of the morning goes to my helpers. Apple, still warm. Don't tell the goose.

hunt.line: Fetch the {items}. Then we're in business!

steps.line: My granddaughter's train comes in this afternoon and I've gone the wrong way twice. She said meet at the place where trains rest and people wave.

steps.hint: Where trains rest and people wave
steps.line: Here we are, and early! He wants flowers for her. A seller near {next} has some.
Sunflowers for a granddaughter, lovely. She told him on the phone they're her favourite. Back to {next}, quick, I hear a whistle.
Oh dear, I've got roses, tulips and sunflowers. Which ones did she say she liked?
steps.wrong: Hmm, Nan said something about her favourite. Big and yellow, I think.
steps.right: Sunflowers, of course. There she is! They're walking home together via {next}.

steps.line: Never once late, thanks to you. Take my old pocket clock, I won't need it, I've got a granddaughter to tell me the time.
A birthday cake needs delivering and my van's a bike with one pedal. It's for someone called Rosie. Her brother is waiting at {next}.
Shh, it's a surprise! Rosie's turning eight and loves anything purple. I lost the candles though, they rolled under something near {next}.
Eight candles, all accounted for. Kai's mum is at {next} with the decorations.
Help me pick the balloons. Which colour will Rosie love?
steps.wrong: Kai pulls a face. Rosie likes one colour above all.
steps.right: Purple everything! Everyone hide at {next}, she's coming!

steps.line: SURPRISE? For me? Purple balloons AND cake? This is the best birthday in the whole history of birthdays.
I'm making a calendar of the town and need helpers in the photos! Twelve months, three helpers, lots of pulling faces. First shot at {next}.
Lovely, that's spring. For summer I want water in the background, and you looking very relaxed.
Perfect summer! Oh no, I dropped my lens cap near {next}. It's tiny and black.
Thank you! Last shot is winter, and Bram wants a cosy spot. Meet at {next}.
That's the year done! You're Miss April, Mr. July and the whole of December. Have this print, a thank-you from the calendar.
My knee's being silly today, would you do my errands? I write my lists as riddles, it keeps the mind sharp. First, go where the bread wakes up early.

steps.hint: Where the bread wakes up early
steps.line: One loaf, warm. Next on her list: 'return the book about the moon'. The book is overdue at {next}.
The moon book! Mrs. Haddad's had it three months, she says it was a long moon. Tell her the sequel's in. Back to {next}.
You're quick! Last test: what did I ask you to return?
steps.wrong: Ha! No, look up at night and you'll remember.
steps.right: The moon! My brain is sharp and my errands are done. Come round to {next}.

steps.line: Bread, books and good company. Here, honey from my sister's bees. Same time next week?
A bouquet of ten balloons got away from me! They're red and floating low. Someone at {next} might've seen them.
Red balloons, yes! Drifted past my ladder an hour ago. One popped on a weathervane, the rest headed for {next}.
Nine balloons, tangled but happy. Clem's customer is waiting at {next}.
I ordered ten balloons for my mum's party. How many are left?
steps.wrong: Count again, Ray saw one meet a weathervane.
steps.right: Nine is perfect, she's ninety, one for each decade! Party's at {next}.

steps.line: Mum loved them. She says the tenth one is on an adventure. Keep this ribbon, for luck.
My van's jingle has gone silent, and without it nobody knows I'm here. The tune's written on a card I keep at {next}.
The card says the jingle starts with three high notes and one low. A music teacher at {next} could help.
Lovely, I'll hum it for you. How does Giorgio's jingle begin?
options: One low note and three high
Three high notes and one low
steps.wrong: That sounds like a doorbell, not ice cream. Check the card again.
steps.right: Ding ding ding, dong! That's the one. Run it back to {next}.

steps.line: The jingle is back and so are the children! Have a little music box, so you never forget the tune.
Welcome to the annual tortoise race! I need a marshal. The champion, Sir Plod, eats only dandelions. His owner is at {next}.
Sir Plod refuses to race without his lucky ribbon. I think it's tucked somewhere near {next}, he likes to hide it.
Lucky ribbon on! Now Dot needs a treat at the finish to keep the racers moving. Head to {next}.
What do we put at the finish line to tempt Sir Plod?
steps.wrong: Sir Plod turns away slowly. Very slowly. He's a picky eater.
steps.right: A dandelion! He's moving. Very slightly. Come watch the finish at {next}.

steps.line: Forty minutes for two metres, a new record! Sir Plod is champion again. A shell-shaped thank you, from the club.
